title: devbin use brew removes its link before asking whether a Homebrew devbin would answer, and can leave none on PATH (contract A4)
body:
`devbin use brew` removes `$HOME/.local/bin/devbin` before it asks whether a Homebrew devbin would answer, so on a machine whose formula is not installed, or whose keg is not linked, it leaves no devbin on PATH. The dev or opt install the link pointed at is still on disk, but nothing names it, and the report that follows ("use: no link, so brew, and Homebrew has no devbin here") comes after the damage. 0.1.14 shipped the same order (0213). hv ruled on 2026-10-26, in vc's session, that this is fixed in 0.1.15, with the dev/opt/brew contract's T5 settled by the signatories first.

## Cause

`lib/cmd/use`'s brew branch checks only that the link is one into a devbin tree, then runs `rm -f "$p"`, and only then calls `_use_report`, which looks for Homebrew's devbin through `devbin_brew_root` (`$HOMEBREW_PREFIX/opt/devbin`) and reports none. `devbin_brew_root` also answers for a keg that is installed but not linked, where no Homebrew `devbin` answers on PATH either. T5 (docs/dev-opt-brew.md) says `use brew` removes the link set so Homebrew's own bin links answer, and says nothing of the case where none would. intent-vc's clarification of 2026-10-25, agreed by the signatories (molt-vc, utilz-vc, intent-vc and gtools-vc) on 2026-10-26 as amendment A4 in intent-vc's wording, adds that `use brew` refuses, removing nothing, when no brew-managed copy would answer once the links are gone (the formula is not installed, its keg is not linked, or another copy comes first on PATH). Intent's `use brew` already asks the first copy on PATH after `~/.local/bin` before removing anything.

## Fix

Before removing the link, the brew branch asks what would answer `devbin` on PATH once the link is gone: the first `devbin` on PATH outside `~/.local/bin`, which must resolve into Homebrew's keg under `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX`. When nothing would answer, or the first copy is not Homebrew's, it refuses with a non-zero exit, removing nothing, and names the link it would have removed, the tree that link serves, why no Homebrew copy would answer (the formula not installed, in `brew_unplaced_why`'s words; its keg not linked; or another copy, named, first on PATH), and the remedies: install or link the formula, or stay on dev or opt, and where another copy comes first, move that copy aside. A link that is not into a devbin tree is still left and named, as now. docs/dev-opt-brew.md's T5 carries the sentence the signatories agree as A4.

## Done when

1. `devbin use brew` refuses with a non-zero exit, names the link, the tree it serves, why no Homebrew copy would answer and the remedies, and leaves the link exactly as it was, in each of three cases: the formula absent; its keg installed but not linked; and another devbin first on PATH ahead of Homebrew's. Each case has an arm, red on main, where the link is removed, and green at the fix.
2. With a linked keg, `use brew` removes the link and reports brew, as now.
3. use.bats passes at the fix under BSD and GNU, beside the tree scans and help.
4. docs/dev-opt-brew.md's T5 carries the agreed A4 sentence.
5. CI's run on the pushed head is green on Test on Ubuntu. That run is this fix's Linux proof, and K115's kovacs verdict carries to the head beside it (hv chose (a), 2026-10-26).

## Resolution

Fixed at f5df4614. cc built it in a scratch clone of main at b2799ae6 (0ba190c2), and vc landed it. Before it removes `~/.local/bin/devbin`, `use brew` now asks `brew_answer_state` (lib/helpers) what would answer `devbin` on PATH once the link is gone: the first `devbin` on PATH, found by bash's own lookup with the link's own directory left out, must resolve to the `bin/devbin` of Homebrew's keg under `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX`. Empty and relative PATH entries are left out too, since each answers from the directory a command is typed in and says nothing of what the machine runs. When the first copy is not Homebrew's, `use brew` exits non-zero, removes nothing, and names the link, the tree it serves, why no Homebrew copy would answer, and that case's remedy, or staying on dev or opt:

- the formula not installed: `brew_unplaced_why`'s clause, and "install devbin with Homebrew", with HOMEBREW_PREFIX exported as `brew shellenv` exports it (0235 landed this remedy as "install devbin with Homebrew (brew install devbin)", a `brew install` hint naming no Linux route beside it, which installhints.bats refuses; 0236 dropped the parenthetical, as devbin's other remedies word it);
- its keg not linked: no `devbin` in Homebrew's bin leads into it, and `brew link devbin`;
- Homebrew's bin not on PATH: its link leads into the keg, and the remedy puts Homebrew's bin on PATH after `~/.local/bin`;
- another `devbin` first on PATH: named, to move aside.

A link into no devbin tree is still refused first, and with a linked keg the link is still removed and brew reported. docs/dev-opt-brew.md's T5 carries amendment A4 in the signatories' wording, and lib/pages/use.md one sentence on the refusal. tests/lib/test_helper.bash gains `path_without`, 0234's PATH hiding as one helper, and targetdir.bats's no-cargo arm moves onto it, so the technique has one copy.

- **Done when 1.** use.bats has an arm for each refusal (the formula absent, its keg not linked, Homebrew's bin off PATH, another devbin first), each checking first that the link is unchanged. On b2799ae6 with cc's first test change alone (83bc4a1f), use.bats under BSD failed each of them at that first check, "use brew removed the link", and failed the A4 arm on "T5 does not carry amendment A4"; no other arm failed. The second pass left those first checks as they were. A further arm, with ./bin first on PATH and a linked keg, failed alone on cc's first build (129b38ff, which still read relative entries), on "use brew left the link". At the fix every one of them passed.
- **Done when 2.** The keg arm, its keg now linked into Homebrew's bin, passed at the fix under BSD and GNU: `use brew` removed the link and reported brew. So did machinepointer.bats's 0197/0213 arm, whose keg is now linked and whose Homebrew bin comes next on PATH.
- **Done when 3.** At the fix (0ba190c2), each file alone, under BSD and then GNU: use.bats, machinepointer.bats, targetdir.bats, help.bats and the tree scans (helpers, contract, neutral, documentation, readonlygit, harness, vendoredmd, workroom). Every TAP ran to its plan with nothing failed, and the only skips were harness.bats's `require_command` arms, which skip by design. targetdir.bats passed again under BSD with 0234's second cargo directory on PATH, so `path_without` still hides a cargo in each entry that holds one. These runs went one at a time under molt-vc's GO for light runs, relayed by vc: a first pass from 2026-10-26 12:27Z to 12:45Z on cc's first build, and a second from 12:55Z to 13:12Z at the fix, after an independent critic-shell review whose smaller findings the fix takes; each ended with rc 0 (~/Devel/scratch/devbin-cc/0235/runs and runs2, sealed in runs.sha256). fleet.bats and releasecut.bats name `use brew` only in text they expect, and no arm of theirs runs it, so they stayed out. Critic leg: `intent critic shell` from the clone's root found nothing at warning or above in lib/cmd/use, lib/helpers and tests/lib/test_helper.bash, for the rules it asked; it asked nothing of the .bats files, so it says nothing about them. installhints.bats, which refuses a vendored hint naming `brew install` without a Linux route on the same line, was in neither these runs nor land235's, and CI run 40331608642 on f06bad4a, the head that landed 0235, failed it at installhints.bats:107 on that remedy; 0236 fixed it.
- **Done when 4.** docs/dev-opt-brew.md's T5 carries A4's sentence, directly after the one on `use brew` removing the whole link set, and a use.bats arm holds it.
- **Done when 5.** CI run 40349359447 on a81f0f98, the head that lands 0236 on top of 0235: green on Test on Ubuntu, this fix's Linux proof; K115's kovacs verdict carries to that head (hv chose (a), 2026-10-26).
